messages.author: 690f07a14d04eab8
messages.subject: Piecewise latent growth curve IRT
parts:
Hello,

I have a longitudinal dataset (3 timepoints) that I want to apply 2PL IRT to. My theory and preliminary analyses show inverse u-shape data show (peaking at the second timepoint). So I think a piecewise latent growth curve IRT might best suit the data (similiar to Kamata, A., Nese, J. F. T., Patarapichayatham, C., & Lai, C.-F. (2013). Modeling Nonlinear Growth With Three Data Points: Illustration With Benchmarking Data. Assessment for Effective Intervention, 38(2), 105–116), with
intercept: t1*1 t2*1 t3*1
slope1: t1*0 t2*1 t3*1
slope2: t1*0 t2*0 t3*1

Is it possible to adapt the linear latent growth curve IRT from https://philchalmers.github.io/mirt/html/Longitudinal-IRT.html into a piecewise latent growth curve IRT?

Cheers,
Kelly

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Piecewise latent growth curve IRT
parts:
Hi Kelly,

Certainly. You likely should only need to organize the set of fixed coefficients either by a) modifying the starting value data.frame prior to estimation or b) using the mirt.model() syntax with the START and FIXED inputs. If you know what coefficients to fix to and how to organize each respective item (which your email suggests you do) then I don't believe you'll have much difficulty in estimating this model using the bfactor() function. HTH, and let us know if you run into any issues.

Phil
